note: _nam commemoratus est inimicorum in imbre, benefacere illis qui ostenderunt rectas vias_ (Vg, NVg) – for he made mention of the enemies under the figure of rain, and of doing good to them that shewed right ways (Douay Version). This sentence is “parfaitement inintelligible” (Lagrange, p. 111). On the basis of the then newly discovered Hebrew text of Sirach, Norbert Peters suggests that the Latin should be _atque etiam commemoratus est Iob, qui amplexus est vias rectas_ – and he (Ezekiel) also referred to Job who embraced the right ways. – Marie-Joseph Lagrange OP: La révision de la Vulgate. _Revue biblique_ nouvelle série 5.1 (1908) 102–113, at pp. 110–111.
